I wonder if it's worth trying a few more combinations just to make it a little more comprehensive. Off the top of my head:

```
ctypedef struct NestedNestedStructMiddle:
    float a
    NestedStructFirst b
    float c

ctypedef struct MultipleNestedNestedStructs1:
    NestedStructFirst a
    NestedStructFirst b
    float c


ctypedef struct MultipleNestedNestedStructs2:
    float a
    NestedStructFirst b
    NestedStructFirst c


ctypedef struct MixedNestedStructs1:
   NestedStructFirst a
   Float3 b

ctypedef struct MixedNestedStructs1:
   Float3 a
   NestedStructFirst b
```

Obviously the existing poor testing isn't entirely your fault but this feels like it might give us a bit more confidence here.

comment_data.body:
I concur that the "special case for complex" probably isn't the right place to fix this. But yes, it's really opaque code. The yet-another-while-loop here makes me wonder whether directly nested structs are really the only issue here, or whether this change only passes the bug on to a different place that we haven't identified yet.

I think I'd feel more comfortable if we could avoid the new while-loop, remove the `break` instead to continue the existing while-loop, and then see under which conditions we need to exit it. I'm not sure that this will lead to a better (or even viable) solution, but it seems more in the spirit of the existing implementation.

It seems reasonable to avoid re-using the complex special case, it was just the easiest way to get something working.

Adding something to the existing while loop is probably better since the comment states that it will push or pop the struct stack. I'm not convinced that avoiding the a while loop would be cleaner, since the existing while loop is focused on advancing the field pointer. You could get away with adding an extra state variable that will skip the advancing of the field pointer right after walking into a struct. Or, setting `ctx->head->field = --field` in the struct case (although this would briefly leave that pointer aimed at something outside of the field list for the relevant type info, which seems a bit iffy)

I'm happy to add some more test cases for doubly nested structs.

I'm not sure the nested struct case warrant's it's own code generator. It might be useful to have a broader buffmt one that covers general mixtures of structs, arrays, strings and different primitives, although that's out of scope of what I'm willing to contribute for this PR.

comment_data.body:
Personally I think I prefer the first. Could also use `goto` instead of `break/continue` to make it clearer where the `continue` is going to.

I'd missed that I'd changed the meaning of `if (field->type->fields->type == NULL) continue; /* empty struct */` in my quick test. Thanks for spotting that.

I think for the sake of this PR some targeted testing of doubly-nested structs is fine and we can add the more comprehensive code generation ourselves if we want to later. It's reasonable for you to have limits to the amount of time you want to put into this.

I prefer the first one, too.
And I second the recommendation for `goto` in the empty struct case for better readability.

EDIT: The "empty struct" condition can move one line up, I think. No need to calculate the `parent_offset` first.
